package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2024-4367) in its font rendering code, which allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript code by embedding malicious commands in PDF font metadata. When a crafted PDF is rendered, this leads to remote code execution in any application or browser context using the vulnerable PDF.js library, enabling full compromise of the host environment.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when rendering a PDF containing a malicious fontMatrix or cmds array
execution_context.file_location: src/display/font_renderer.js (core font rendering logic in pdfjs-dist)
required_permissions: JavaScript execution in the rendering context
Access to PDF metadata (fontMatrix, cmds arrays)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a PDF with attacker-controlled font metadata is rendered, the code dynamically constructs a JavaScript function using the Function constructor, directly incorporating commands from the PDF's cmds array, resulting in execution of arbitrary JavaScript code supplied by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code uses the Function constructor to generate executable JavaScript from PDF font metadata (cmds), which can be controlled by an attacker. This allows injection and execution of arbitrary code if a malicious PDF is processed.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal PDF rendering should safely interpret font and drawing commands from document metadata without ever executing them as JavaScript code. Executing untrusted PDF content as code violates the security boundary between document data and application logic.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic function generation may be used for performance optimization in trusted, internal code where all inputs are strictly validated and sanitized, but never with untrusted user-supplied data such as PDF metadata.
key_indicators: Use of new Function with input derived from PDF file content (cmds array)
No sanitization or validation of cmds before code generation
Direct mapping of PDF metadata to executable JavaScript statements
Function constructor invoked within font rendering logic
Console output of dynamically generated JavaScript code during rendering

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious PDF with a fontMatrix or cmds array containing JavaScript code as a string.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious data is loaded by the PDF.js renderer.

attack_chain.action: PDF.js processes the PDF and passes the attacker-controlled cmds to the font rendering logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: cmds array is used to generate JavaScript code.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code dynamically constructs a function using the Function constructor with the attacker-controlled cmds.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary JavaScript code is executed in the context of the application or browser.

attack_chain.action: Attacker's code runs with the privileges of the application, potentially leading to data theft, further exploitation, or system compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: remote code execution and compromise of the host environment.

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic function generation (new Function) with input derived from PDF file content (cmds or fontMatrix arrays)
Execution of JavaScript code embedded in PDF font metadata during rendering
Unexpected alert(), eval(), or network requests triggered during PDF rendering
Console output of dynamically generated JavaScript code in PDF.js font rendering
file_indicators: PDF files with non-numeric or string values in fontMatrix or cmds arrays
Presence of pdf.js or pdfjs-dist versions below 4.2.67 in node_modules or application bundles
PDF files containing suspicious JavaScript code fragments in font-related metadata
network_indicators: Outbound network requests initiated during PDF rendering (e.g., attacker code exfiltrates data)
Unusual connections to domains or IPs not associated with normal PDF.js operation, triggered during PDF processing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for use of the Function constructor or eval in PDF.js code paths, especially where input is derived from PDF file content. Scan PDF files for suspicious fontMatrix or cmds values containing JavaScript code or non-numeric entries. Audit application dependencies for vulnerable pdfjs-dist versions. Implement runtime protections such as Content Security Policy (CSP) to block dynamic code execution in PDF rendering contexts. Use behavioral monitoring to detect unexpected JavaScript execution or network activity during PDF rendering.
